column7: 2026-11-04: parseBytes (named export in index.js): only plain numbers + binary units (KiB..YiB), case-sensitive. kB/MB/GB etc. deliberately throw 'Unsupported unit' until user confirms with the storage team how to read them. Fractions truncated to whole bytes; signs/exponents rejected.

2026-11-04: Storage team answer (for the follow-up): non-i units are powers of 1024 on this branch because their users paste sizes from Windows Explorer. 1 KB or kB = 1024, 1 MB = 1048576, etc. Not implemented yet; kB/MB/... still throw. Note this differs from prettyBytes' SI output (1 kB = 1000) on purpose.

2026-11-04: billing-svc already sits at aee79d7 (same commit as storage-app) which has parseBytes with tests and types; nothing new was needed. kB/MB/GB still throw pending the storage team's answer (see decision 252f7f1); billing only wants binary units so it can stay that way.

2026-11-04: billing-svc parseBytes also accepts SI units kB..YB as powers of 1000 (1 MB = 1000000, matches prettyBytes; billing quotes strict SI). Differs from storage-app, which plans 1024 for non-i units, so do not merge/copy that reading across. Case-sensitive: KB, mB, Mb, kbit still throw. Conversion uses BigInt so 0.29 kB is exactly 290 (float gave 289).

2026-11-04: parseBytes now accepts non-i units (kB, KB, MB..YB) as powers of 1024, per the storage team (Windows Explorer paste). Case-sensitive: kB and KB both OK, mB/Kb/kb rejected. Readme and index.d.ts warn that this differs from prettyBytes' SI output, so parseBytes(prettyBytes(1500)) != 1500. Done; not committed.
